mainTopic: Why the decree against dodging obligations through a non-Jew covers תרומה but not חלה, and the משנה of the עומר offering with רבי יהודה's view on preparing new flour
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about the Rabbis' decree that grain processed while owned by a non-Jew still needs תרומה and מעשר. That decree stops people from putting their grain in a non-Jew's name to avoid giving. The גמרא asks why חלה is not included in the decree. It answers that dough is easy to exempt anyway, just by baking less than the minimum amount. It then objects that תרומה also has easy ways out, such as רבי אושעיא's trick or bringing grain in over the roofs. The answer is that those tricks are public and embarrassing, while baking small batches is private. A new משנה then describes how the כהן offered the עומר. It ends with a מחלוקת: once the עומר was offered, the ירושלים market was already full of new flour, and רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue whether the חכמים approved. The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה isn't worried people will eat the flour early, since in בדיקת חמץ he does worry about this. רבה begins to answer that חדש is different, and his reason continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not make the same decree for חלה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the Rabbis' decree is not also applied to חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is the reason for the decree, then חלה should be included in it too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason it just gave for the decree on תרומה. If the worry is people dodging their obligation through a non-Jew, the same worry should apply to dough and חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the Rabbis obligated grain processed while owned by a non-Jew, so people would not hand their grain to a non-Jew to escape תרומה. Dough kneaded while owned by a non-Jew, however, is exempt from חלה. Since someone could dodge חלה the same way, the decree seems to be missing a case.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is the reasoning
The portion of dough given to a כהן
Also; too

phrases.english: If so,
then even challah too [should be included]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason for the decree given just before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason for the decree on grain processed by a non-Jew
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the decree exists to stop people from dodging obligations through a non-Jew, it should cover חלה as well, yet dough kneaded by a non-Jew is exempt.

steps.title: Dough can be exempted more easily by baking small batches
steps.stepSummary: There is no need for a decree on חלה, because a person can simply bake less than the amount that requires חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person who wants to avoid חלה can just bake with less than five quarters of a קב of flour and a bit more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that no decree is needed for חלה. Someone who wants to avoid it has a much simpler way than going through a non-Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dough only requires חלה if it is at least a set amount of flour. A person can avoid the obligation completely, and legally, by making smaller batches. So nobody would bother with the non-Jew trick for dough, and the Rabbis had nothing to block.

keyTerms.meaning: It is possible
Five quarters (of a קב), the minimum amount of flour for חלה
Flour

phrases.english: It is possible for him to bake it
with less than five quarters of flour and a bit more.
phrases.notes: Five quarters of a קב plus a little extra is the smallest amount of dough that needs חלה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶפְשָׁר דְּאָפֵי לָהּ פָּחוֹת מֵחֲמֵשֶׁת רְבָעִים קֶמַח, וְעוֹד
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical distinction: an easier way to avoid the obligation already exists
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree should cover חלה just as it covers תרומה
steps.terutzMaskana: Since חלה can easily be avoided by baking small batches, no one would use a non-Jew, so no decree is needed

steps.title: תרומה can also be avoided easily
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: תרומה and מעשר can also be avoided easily, through רבי אושעיא's trick or by bringing grain in over roofs.
steps.simpleTranslation: תרומה can also be avoided, like רבי אושעיא taught: a person may bring his grain in still in its chaff, so his animal can eat it without מעשר. Or he can bring it in over the roofs or through enclosures. So why was a decree needed for תרומה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the last answer against the decree on תרומה. If an easy way out means no decree is needed, then תרומה has easy ways out too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 said a decree is pointless when there is a simpler legal way to avoid the obligation. But grain also has simple ways out: bring it in before it is fully processed, or bring it in without passing through the house's entrance. So by the same logic, the decree on תרומה should be unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן
Uses a legal trick to avoid an obligation
Chaff, the husk around the grain
Tithe
Enclosed open areas, not the main entrance of a house

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying תרומה has no obligation. It is asking why the Rabbis needed a decree, if people already have easy legal ways out.

phrases.english: Teruma too,
it is possible for him to act like Rabbi Oshaya [taught]?
As Rabbi Oshaya said:
A person may use a trick with his grain
and bring it in with its chaff,
so that his animal may eat [it]
and it is exempt from tithes.
Alternatively, he can bring it in
by way of roofs or by way of enclosures?
phrases.notes: The idea is that produce becomes obligated when it comes in through the house's entrance, so going around it avoids the obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרוּמָה נָמֵי, אֶפְשָׁר דְּעָבֵיד לַהּ כִּדְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the logic of the answer in step 2 against the decree on תרומה
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 2, and the need for a decree on תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an easy way to avoid the obligation makes a decree unnecessary, תרומה also has easy ways out, so it should not need a decree either.

steps.title: Public tricks are embarrassing, private ones are not
steps.stepSummary: The tricks for avoiding תרומה are done in public and are embarrassing, so people would prefer the non-Jew method. Baking small batches is private, so people would use it instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, with תרומה, the tricks are done in public, and that is embarrassing. Here, with חלה, it is done in private, and that is not embarrassing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by comparing how public each trick is. That explains why a decree was needed for תרומה but not for חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bringing grain in with its chaff, or over the roofs, can be seen by everyone, and a person would be ashamed to be seen dodging. So he would choose the quieter non-Jew method, and the Rabbis blocked it with a decree. Baking small batches happens inside the home, so people would just do that, and no decree was needed for חלה.

keyTerms.meaning: In public
In private
It is degrading or embarrassing for him
There / here; used to compare two cases

steps.whatToRemember: The decree against using a non-Jew to avoid obligations covers תרומה and מעשר, because the other ways out are public and embarrassing. It does not cover חלה, because making small batches of dough is private and easy.

phrases.english: There, it is in public,
[so] it is degrading for him;
here, it is in private,
[so] it is not degrading for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם בְּפַרְהֶסְיָא, זִילָא בֵּיהּ מִילְּתָא; הָכָא בְּצִינְעָא, לָא זִילָא בֵּיהּ מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 and supports the answer of step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the cases: public versus private
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any easy way out makes a decree unnecessary, so תרומה should not need one
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a private, non-embarrassing way out makes a decree unnecessary. The tricks for תרומה are public, so the decree is needed there.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the Rabbis made decrees based on how people actually behave. They blocked only the loophole people would really use.

steps.title: משנה: How the כהן offered the עומר
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה describes the steps of offering the מנחת העומר, ending with the כהנים eating the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהן came to the tenth of an איפה of flour. He put its oil and frankincense on it, poured and mixed, waved it and brought it to the altar, took a handful and burned it. The rest is eaten by the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes, step by step, how the כהן offered the עומר once the flour was ready.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of these steps match a regular מנחה: oil and frankincense, pouring and mixing, bringing it near, taking the handful (קמיצה) and burning it. The waving (תנופה) is an extra step that only a few מנחות have, the עומר among them. The leftover flour goes to the כהנים to eat, just like other flour offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין: our משנה
A tenth of an איפה, the measure of flour for the עומר
Frankincense
Waved it and brought it near to the altar
Took a handful of the מנחה to burn on the altar

phrases.english: MISHNA: He came to the tenth [of an ephah],
phrases.notes: This is the flour for the עומר, the tenth of an איפה that was prepared before this point.

phrases.english: put on it its oil and its frankincense,
poured and mixed,
waved and brought [it] near,
took the handful and burned [it],
and the rest is eaten by the priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה; it begins a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עומר is offered with oil and frankincense, pouring and mixing, waving and bringing near, taking a handful and burning it. The rest is eaten by the כהנים.

steps.title: Market full of new flour right after the offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends with a מחלוקת. רבי מאיר says the חכמים did not approve of preparing new-grain flour before the עומר. רבי יהודה says they did approve.
steps.simpleTranslation: As soon as the עומר was offered, people went out and found the ירושלים market already full of flour from roasted grain. רבי מאיר says this was done without the חכמים' approval. רבי יהודה says it was done with their approval.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its description of the עומר with a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. They disagree about whether the חכמים approved of the full market.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The market was full the very moment the עומר was offered. So the grain must have been harvested, roasted and ground while חדש was still forbidden to eat. רבי מאיר says the חכמים did not like this. רבי יהודה says they allowed it.

keyTerms.meaning: The marketplace of ירושלים
Flour made from roasted (parched) grain
With the approval of the חכמים
From the moment it was offered

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody here is talking about eating the flour before the עומר. Both sides agree eating it is forbidden. They only argue about whether preparing and selling it ahead of time was approved.

phrases.english: Once the omer was offered,
they would go out and find the market of Jerusalem
full of flour from roasted grain,
phrases.notes: If it was full that fast, the flour had to be made before the עומר, while new grain was still off-limits.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא בִּרְצוֹן חֲכָמִים – דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: not with the approval of the Sages; these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בִּרְצוֹן חֲכָמִים הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: They would do it with the approval of the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁקָּרַב הָעוֹמֶר, יוֹצְאִין וּמוֹצְאִין שׁוּק יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה from step 5 with a closing מחלוקת about the market.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר says filling the market with new-grain flour before the עומר was not approved. רבי יהודה says it was approved.

steps.title: Isn't רבי יהודה worried people will eat it early?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה doesn't make a גזירה against preparing the flour, out of fear that people will eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't רבי יהודה make a גזירה here, out of worry that someone will come to eat from the flour?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a challenge to רבי יהודה. It asks why he isn't afraid that people handling forbidden flour will end up eating it. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא brings proof that he usually does worry about this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pile of flour that is forbidden right now, sitting in the market, is easy to nibble from. Normally the חכמים would forbid handling it to protect people. So רבי יהודה's approval looks surprising.

keyTerms.meaning: Made a rabbinic decree (גזירה) as a protective fence
Perhaps he will come to eat (it)
From it

phrases.english: GEMARA:
And doesn't Rabbi Yehuda make a decree
lest one come to eat from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא גָּזַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה דִּלְמָא אָתֵי לְמֵיכַל מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's opinion from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that preparing new-grain flour before the עומר was approved.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Handling forbidden food usually calls for a גזירה, so it can't lead to eating. Why doesn't רבי יהודה make one here?

steps.title: רבי יהודה does worry about eating, in checking for חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from פסחים. It shows that רבי יהודה does not allow checking for חמץ once the time to destroy it has passed, out of concern that the person will eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can point to a contradiction. רבי יהודה says you check for חמץ on the night of the fourteenth, on the morning of the fourteenth, and at the time of destroying the חמץ. The חכמים say: if he did not check at night, he checks later, even during the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings evidence that sharpens its question. In בדיקת חמץ, רבי יהודה does make a protective rule because of the fear of eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה stops the checking at the time of destroying the חמץ, and the חכמים let it go on into פסח. That shows רבי יהודה fears a person who finds חמץ during פסח might eat it. If he worries there, why not with new-grain flour?

keyTerms.meaning: "And contrast them": the גמרא sets two sources against each other
We search (for חמץ)
The night of the 14th of ניסן
The time of destroying the חמץ

phrases.english: And contrast them:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, בּוֹדְקִין אוֹר אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: One searches on the night of the fourteenth,
and on the fourteenth in the morning,
and at the time of destroying the leaven,
phrases.notes: After that, רבי יהודה stops. He won't let you search during פסח itself.

phrases.english: And the Sages say: If he did not search, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." cuts the משנה short. The rest says he checks on the 14th, and if not, during the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that makes the question in step 7 a real contradiction.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה normally makes a גזירה because of the fear that someone will eat forbidden food.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in פסחים about the times for בדיקת חמץ.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling in our משנה that filling the market with new-grain flour before the עומר was approved
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In פסחים, רבי יהודה stops the search for חמץ at the time of destroying it, because he fears a person who finds חמץ on פסח will eat it. By that logic he should also fear people eating new-grain flour before the עומר, and so forbid preparing it.

steps.title: רבה: new grain is different
steps.stepSummary: רבה begins to answer that חדש is different from חמץ. His reason continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: חדש (new grain) is different.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה starts answering the contradiction by saying the case of חדש is not like the case of חמץ. This line only sets up the answer. The actual reason comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה does not say רבי יהודה stopped worrying about eating. He says something special about חדש makes a גזירה unnecessary there. Keep that in mind as the explanation unfolds.

keyTerms.meaning: Is different
New grain, forbidden to eat until the עומר is offered

phrases.english: Rabba said: New grain is different,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the contradiction raised in steps 7-8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה's worry about eating חמץ should carry over to חדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: חדש is different, so the חמץ ruling does not carry over. The reason continues on the next amud.
